why: Run 34413372916 rendered sixteen families in one batch. Nine receipts were carried and verified within minutes and then waited, because the importer requires the RUN OBJECT to report completed/success before it will admit anything, and the run does not close until its longest job does. A two-page Kentucky family sat behind a thirty-eight-page Louisiana one. Nothing was lost and nothing was rerun, but nine families were admissible and idle.
theRequirementThatCausesItAndStays: The importer refuses with 'ValueError: central run failed' while the run is in progress, and it is right to. A receipt from a run that later fails is not evidence. The consuming lane proved this deliberately rather than assuming it, and admitted nothing until the run closed. That requirement is not being relaxed.
theRule: Group a dispatch into modest batches by EXPECTED PAGE COUNT, read from the raster queue's own rows rather than guessed.
Keep a batch's longest job within roughly the same order of magnitude as its shortest. Two to eight pages in one batch, ten to twenty in another, thirty and up in a third.
Prefer several small runs to one large one when the spread is wide. Each run closes on its own longest job, so a narrow spread is the whole point.
Never rerun an admitted output to reorganise a completed batch. An admitted receipt is bound to bytes that have not moved, and re-rendering it buys nothing and costs a receipt.
whatThisIsNot: Not a scheduler and not a queue. It is how a family_batch input is chosen, and it changes only the grouping of a dispatch that would have happened anyway.
